source_text: While proponents in affected communities may view Gishiri cutting as a remedial intervention rather than mutilation, the classification prioritizes anatomical injury and absence of evidence-based efficacy, as evidenced by studies linking it to severe outcomes like genital fistulas without proven preventive value.
